subject: PE & Wellbeing
source: National Curriculum (Physical Education); UK Chief Medical Officers' physical activity guidelines. Drive PE folder reviewed (TSS Long-Term PE Plan: fitness, fair play, leadership, resilience) and adapted to at-home, no-equipment, no-contact lessons.

lessons.title: Components of fitness
objectives: Name and define five components of fitness
Match an exercise to each component
Test one component safely at home

keywords.def: the ability to keep going for a long time
how much force your muscles can produce
how far your joints can move
changing direction quickly and under control

starter: Bismillah. Why do we warm up?

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Stop if you feel pain or dizziness
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: Five components
teach.note: Show a card for each. Ask pupils to give a sport for each. Common mistake: fitness is just running.

teach.heading: Matching exercises
teach.note: Ask which component does a star jump train. Discuss that many exercises train more than one.

teach.heading: Home tests
bullets: Stamina: jog on the spot for 2 minutes
Strength: how many squats in 30 seconds
Flexibility: sit and reach with a ruler
teach.note: Keep tests gentle and non-competitive; compare with their own earlier result. Avoid comparing pupils.

teach.heading: Record and reflect
bullets: Which would you like to improve?
teach.note: Pupils record in a table. Teach that fitness grows with regular practice.

independent: Match four exercises to the correct component.
Complete a 30-second squat test and record it.
exit: Complete your three tests and write a short table of results.
Choose one component to improve and say how.
homework: Which component does jogging mainly train?
lessons.send: Repeat one test later in the week and compare your result.

lessons.title: Circuit training and checking your pulse
objectives: Perform a circuit with good technique
Measure pulse at rest and after exercise

keywords.def: the beat of your heart felt in your wrist or neck
your pulse when you are calm and still
how quickly your pulse returns to normal

starter: Where do we feel the pulse?

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Stop if you feel sick, dizzy or sore
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: Finding your pulse
bullets: Count beats for 15 seconds, times four
teach.note: Model finding the pulse on the thumb side of the inside wrist. Practise at rest. Common error: using the thumb, which has its own pulse.

teach.heading: Resting pulse
teach.note: Record. A child's resting pulse is often higher than an adult's, so do not compare to adults.

teach.heading: The circuit
teach.note: Time stations. Coach technique: soft landings, straight back, controlled squats.

teach.heading: Pulse after exercise
bullets: Check it again after two minutes
teach.note: Discuss why the pulse rose and then fell. Link to heart pumping more oxygen to muscles.

practice: How do you find your pulse?
independent: Take your resting pulse and record it.
Do two stations and take your pulse again.
exit: Complete the full circuit and record the pulse before, straight after, and two minutes later.
Write two sentences explaining the pattern.
homework: Why does your pulse increase with exercise?
lessons.send: Take your resting pulse every morning for three days.
